A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiHeadDepth and HomoDepth research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix 7.5 report original depth-estimation accuracy, latency, quantization, and homography-noise experiments.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain original empirical results and add Middlebury evaluation, perspective-transformed SceneFlow results, and additional comparisons.

M1.justification: The written depth loss in Equation 6 changes gradient subsampling levels from 1–5 to 0–4. Algorithm 1 also moves pointwise convolution outside the head loop. The principal architectures remain unchanged; LND names the existing LayerNorm-plus-dot operation. These revisions do not establish that implementations or training runs changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds Middlebury 2014 stereo images and perspective-transformed SceneFlow simulating camera misalignment. These extend coverage within the existing stereo-depth task; SceneFlow, ADT, DTU, and DTUdf remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Selective-Stereo while retaining the four original depth-model comparators. New Figure 2 also evaluates the proposed similarity approximation against cosine similarity, BatchNorm-plus-dot, and plain dot.

E3.justification: Added protocols include training on SceneFlow and testing on Middlebury, perspective-transforming SceneFlow, and comparing dataset-averaged similarity maps at offset 10 after rescaling. Existing input resolution, evaluation metrics, and appendix dataset splits are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds evidence about the choice of similarity normalization, and Table 4 extends the rectification ablation to simulated camera misalignment. Existing quantization, DTUdf, and homography-noise sensitivity analyses remain; the latter is redisplayed rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 9b replaces Figure 7b’s mean values, standard-deviation curve, and linear fit with boxplots showing loss ranges and outliers. The accompanying prose still references standard deviations and linear fitting. Neither version supplies training seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: New results include Middlebury MultiHeadDepth AbsRel of 0.094, Selective-Stereo comparisons, and SceneFlowpersp HomoDepth AbsRel of 0.097. Existing accuracy entries remain unchanged. GPU reporting also changes substantially: Figure 8 plots Argos near 7 ms instead of v1’s 109 ms, reversing its ranking against MultiHeadDepth, and replaces MobileStereoNet memory-failure entries with numeric points. No corresponding setting change explains these differences.

T1.justification: Equation 6 changes the mathematical loss definition by including subsampling levels 0–4 instead of 1–5; the definition of each level remains unchanged. The homography derivations, positional encoding, complexity arguments, and metric formulas otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and abstract improvement ranges remain unchanged. The introduction removes the separate claim of a 7% AbsRel reduction while retaining the corresponding 25% latency-reduction claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds an accuracy-versus-computation interpretation relative to Selective-Stereo and qualifies Argos’s advantage over DynamicStereo as applying to one-shot estimation. Existing application recommendations are retained, moving from the conclusion to Appendix F.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-availability statement and repository link. Section 5.2 newly specifies batch size 10, no learning-rate scheduler, and checkpoint selection, and revises the reported RTX 4090 memory from 32 GB to 24 GB. These are documentation changes without evidence of rerunning existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Selective-Stereo, Middlebury 2014, Fast R-CNN, and LayerNorm documentation. Argos remains the central reference model. Several other reference edits update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, related work, method explanations, and evaluation prose are rewritten. v2 introduces LND terminology, adds acknowledgments, reorganizes Appendix 7.1–7.5 into Appendices A–E, and moves application guidance into Appendix F.

P2.justification: v2 adds similarity maps and performance-tradeoff plots, redraws architecture and positional-encoding figures, and reorganizes several tables. Table 2 loses its numerical efficiency rows as Figure 8 supplies graphical comparisons. The appendix sensitivity plot changes from scatter/curve displays to boxplots.

improvement.justification: Added transfer and misalignment tests, Selective-Stereo comparisons, and implementation details strengthen the paper. However, Figure 8 introduces unexplained GPU results: Argos appears near 7 ms despite 109 ms remaining in Table 4, reversing its latency ranking against MultiHeadDepth. This inconsistency affects the central efficiency evidence. The gains and reporting harm prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
